scope: Every back/front RGBA color/light buffer SHA256 and nonzero count, exact source lifecycle, actor state and hook stream. Baseline and alternate seed/palette/options/camera fixtures. Finite deterministic fixtures are not a universal proof for all possible parameter values. No website background/actor or GPU camera-response equality is claimed.
implementation: Direct typed source-algorithm port with Float32Array coercion
preview_scope: CPU diagnostic preview reconstructed from verified shared Frame: back draw, synthetic actor color blit when configured, front draw; add combined light once, then combined color. Not a viewport recording.

presentation.native_viewport_scope: Shared Canvas path independently passed the Pickup 24-state actual viewport gate. Effect-specific native viewport recording/review is separate from these source-combined-buffer tests.
presentation.layout_scope: The footer-only host revision retains the frame, draw order, origins, scale, simulation parameters and clocks. Combined hashes in this report were checked with combined_test_host_sha256. The new footer passed 20 font-layout states, and Pickup plus both Sparkle modes retained all 366 combined hashes.

lifecycle_revision.evidence_scope: Previously recorded full raw-buffer parity and native captures use historical_native_sha256 (or the unchanged Fog hash). This revision adds only configure-before-replacement disposal and passed bounded same-instance reuse tests; no full weather replay is claimed.

focused_sampling.scope: Four deterministic Float32 fields, IEEE boundary hex and deterministic fractional coordinates; NaN equivalence; signed zero bits.

combined_source.scope: Original TS shared Frame back/front drawing, source options and camera; no synthetic actor requested by either Fog fixture.

native_live.method: Predeclared serial A1/B1/B2/A2, 60 original source ticks each, ordinary engine time, no recorder
native_live.scope: Terminal hashes are not a new per-frame viewport pixel comparison. Software-renderer bounded observation; about 309.05ms per tick, not real-time or all-platform guarantee.
